column1: 1:1|In the eighth month of Darius’s second year, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:|Retains date and both ancestral names without deciding the title’s grammatical attachment beyond the familiar apposition.
1:2|“The LORD was very angry with your ancestors.|Preserves the emphatic anger opening.

1:3|Tell them: The LORD of Armies says, ‘Return to me,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘and I will return to you,’ says the LORD of Armies.|Retains all three divine-name formulas and the return/return reciprocity.

1:4|‘Do not be like your ancestors. The earlier prophets called to them: The LORD of Armies says, “Turn back from your evil ways and evil deeds.” But they would not listen or pay attention to me,’ declares the LORD.|Keeps ways/deeds paired and makes the nested prophetic speech clear.
1:5|‘Your ancestors—where are they? And the prophets—do they live forever?|Retains both questions without supplying answers.

1:6|But did not my words and decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets, overtake your ancestors?’ Then they turned back and said, ‘The LORD of Armies has done to us just as he planned, in keeping with our ways and deeds.’”|Keeps the overtaking image and repeated ways/deeds in the response.

1:7|On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in Darius’s second year, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:|Preserves all date details and repeats the full prophetic identification.

1:8|During the night I saw a man riding a red horse. He stood among the myrtle trees in the hollow, with red, sorrel, and white horses behind him.|Retains the rider, hollow, myrtles, and three colors without identifying symbolic nations.
1:9|I asked, “What are these, my lord?” The angel speaking with me answered, “I will show you what they are.”|Distinguishes the interpreting angel from the seen rider while preserving the question.
1:10|The man standing among the myrtles said, “These are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth.”|Keeps the rider’s reply and earthly patrol.

1:11|They answered the angel of the LORD standing among the myrtles: “We have patrolled the earth, and look—the whole earth is settled and quiet.”|Preserves the report’s troubling peace without equating it with justice.

1:12|Then the angel of the LORD said, “LORD of Armies, how long will you withhold compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which you have been angry these seventy years?”|Retains intercession, both regions, and the exact seventy years.
1:13|The LORD answered the angel speaking with me with good words, words of comfort.|Retains the repeated words and comforting answer.

1:14|The angel speaking with me said, “Proclaim this: The LORD of Armies says, ‘I am deeply jealous for Jerusalem and Zion.|Keeps jealousy and both city designations rather than replacing with generic concern.
1:15|I am very angry with the nations at ease. I was angry for a little while, but they made the harm worse.’|Preserves the contrast between divine anger and the nations’ aggravation of harm.

1:16|So the LORD says, ‘I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be rebuilt within her,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.’|Keeps restoration, rebuilding, and measuring as distinct actions.

1:17|Proclaim again: The LORD of Armies says, ‘My cities will again overflow with good things. The LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.’”|Retains the repeated again and both comfort and choice.
1:18|I looked up and saw four horns.|Keeps the count and unexplained initial vision image.
1:19|I asked the angel speaking with me, “What are these?” He answered, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”|Preserves all three named communities in the interpretation.
1:20|Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.|Keeps the matching count without narrowing the craft prematurely.

1:21|I asked, “What have they come to do?” He answered, “Those horns scattered Judah so thoroughly that no one could lift his head. These have come to terrify them and throw down the horns of the nations that raised a horn against Judah’s land to scatter it.”|Retains head and horn imagery and explains the action’s referents through demonstratives.
2:1|I looked up and saw a man with a measuring cord in his hand.|Retains the repeated viewing formula and concrete measuring implement.
2:2|I asked, “Where are you going?” He answered, “To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide and how long it is.”|Keeps both dimensions and the intended action.
2:3|Then the angel speaking with me went out, and another angel came out to meet him.|Maintains two angels without merging their roles.

2:4|He said to him, “Run and tell that young man: ‘Jerusalem will be inhabited like open country because of the many people and animals within her.|Retains the unwalled-settlement image and includes animals in abundance.
2:5|I myself will be a wall of fire around her,’ declares the LORD, ‘and I will be glory within her.’”|Keeps the two forms of divine presence, surrounding and within.

2:6|“Come! Come! Flee from the land of the north,” declares the LORD. “For I have spread you out like the four winds of heaven,” declares the LORD.|Retains the repeated summons and four-winds comparison.
2:7|“Come, Zion! Escape, you who live with daughter Babylon!”|Preserves the two city personifications and exile setting.

2:8|For the LORD of Armies says—after glory he sent me to the nations that plundered you—“Whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.|Keeps the difficult after-glory clause, sent speaker, and his-eye pronoun without silent harmonization.

2:9|I will wave my hand over them, and they will become plunder for their own slaves.” Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me.|Retains the reversal between enslavers and slaves and the recognition formula.
2:10|“Sing and rejoice, daughter Zion! I am coming, and I will dwell among you,” declares the LORD.|Keeps direct promise, dwelling, and feminine personification.

2:11|“Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day and become my people. I will dwell among you.” Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me to you.|Preserves the consequential shifts among LORD, my, I, and me rather than deciding the speaker’s identity in translation.
2:12|The LORD will take Judah as his own portion in the holy land and will again choose Jerusalem.|Retains inheritance language, holy land, and renewed choice.
2:13|Be silent before the LORD, all flesh! He has stirred from his holy dwelling.|Keeps the all-flesh address and awakening image.

3:1|He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with the accuser at his right hand to accuse him.|Retains the accuser’s role and its repeated verb without prematurely imposing a proper name.

3:2|The LORD said to the accuser, “The LORD rebuke you, accuser! The LORD who chooses Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a burning stick snatched from the fire?”|Keeps all three LORD occurrences and the rescued-brand question.
3:3|Joshua stood before the angel wearing filthy clothes.|Preserves the concrete clothing and position.

3:4|The angel told those standing before him, “Take off his filthy clothes.” Then he said to Joshua, “See, I have removed your guilt from you, and I will dress you in fine robes.”|Distinguishes command to attendants from assurance to Joshua and connects guilt with clothing removal.

3:5|I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So they placed a clean turban on his head and dressed him, while the angel of the LORD stood nearby.|Follows the pinned I-said reading and preserves the prophet’s participation.
3:6|The angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua:|Retains the solemn transition to conditional instruction.

3:7|“The LORD of Armies says, ‘If you walk in my ways and keep my charge, you will govern my house and guard my courts. I will give you access among these who stand here.|Preserves both conditions and both responsibilities, with access among attendants left unexplained.

3:8|Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions seated before you—for they are men who serve as signs. I am bringing my servant, the Branch.|Keeps sign-men and the Branch title without identifying its fulfillment.

3:9|Look at the stone I have set before Joshua: on that one stone are seven eyes. I will engrave its inscription,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘and I will remove the guilt of that land in a single day.|Retains one stone, seven eyes, inscription, and single day as distinct details.
3:10|On that day,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘each of you will invite his neighbor under his vine and fig tree.’”|Keeps the concrete peace-and-hospitality image.
4:1|The angel speaking with me returned and roused me, as someone is awakened from sleep.|Preserves the simile rather than declaring the vision a dream.

4:2|He asked, “What do you see?” I answered, “A lampstand entirely of gold, with a bowl on top and seven lamps on it, and seven channels for each of the lamps on top.|Follows the read I-answered form and renders the repeated seven distributively, with the construction noted.
4:3|Beside it are two olive trees, one to the bowl’s right and one to its left.”|Retains exact bilateral arrangement.
4:4|I asked the angel speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”|Keeps the question open rather than substituting an interpretation.
4:5|He answered, “Do you not know what these are?” “No, my lord,” I said.|Makes the exchange easy to follow while preserving both responses.

4:6|He said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: ‘Not by military strength, nor by power, but by my spirit,’ says the LORD of Armies.|Distinguishes force from power and retains the central spirit contrast.

4:7|Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground. He will bring out the top stone amid shouts of ‘Grace, grace to it!’”|Keeps mountain, top stone, and the repeated grace acclamation.
4:8|The word of the LORD came to me:|Retains the new prophetic-word introduction.

4:9|“Zerubbabel’s hands laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me to you.|Retains repeated hands, beginning/completion, and sent-speaker formula.

4:10|Who has despised the day of small things? These seven will rejoice when they see the plumb stone in Zerubbabel’s hand. They are the eyes of the LORD, ranging through the whole earth.”|Connects seven to the eyes while retaining the uncertain tin/plumb stone image in a note.
4:11|I asked him, “What are these two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand?”|Retains the repeated question and positions.
4:12|I asked him a second time, “What are the two olive branches beside the two golden pipes that pour out the gold?”|Preserves literal gold rather than silently substituting oil in the vision.
4:13|He said, “Do you not know what these are?” “No, my lord,” I answered.|Keeps the repeated ignorance-and-answer exchange.

4:14|He said, “These are the two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”|Renders the sons-of-oil idiom as anointed ones; retains the literal expression in the note without assigning the figures identities.
5:1|Again I looked up and saw a flying scroll.|Keeps the recurring look and the surprising object.
5:2|He asked me, “What do you see?” I answered, “A flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.”|Retains exact numbers and ancient units.

5:3|He said, “This is the curse going out over the whole land. Every thief will be swept away according to what is on one side, and everyone who swears will be swept away according to what is on the other.|Chooses swept-away and two-sided reading for difficult wording, with alternatives identified in notes.

5:4|I have sent it out,” declares the LORD of Armies. “It will enter the thief’s house and the house of anyone who swears falsely by my name. It will stay inside that house and consume it, timbers and stones alike.”|Retains the curse’s entering, remaining, and consuming actions and both materials.
5:5|The angel speaking with me came forward and said, “Look up and see what is coming out.”|Keeps the new vision summons distinct.

5:6|I asked, “What is it?” He answered, “An ephah basket coming out.” He added, “This is their appearance throughout the land.”|Preserves ephah and the pinned eye/appearance reading rather than silently changing to iniquity.
5:7|A lead cover was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the ephah basket.|Retains the woman, material, and container without allegorical expansion.
5:8|He said, “This is Wickedness.” He pushed her back into the ephah basket and threw the lead weight over its opening.|Retains the explicit personification and forceful confinement.

5:9|I looked up and saw two women coming forward, with wind in their wings. Their wings were like a stork’s. They lifted the ephah basket between earth and heaven.|Keeps female winged figures, the stork comparison, and the airborne position.
5:10|I asked the angel speaking with me, “Where are they taking the ephah basket?”|Preserves the destination question rather than anticipating its answer.

5:11|He answered, “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar. When it is ready, the basket will be set there on its base.”|Retains Shinar and installation on a base without asserting an unstated cultic identification.
6:1|Again I looked up and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains. The mountains were made of bronze.|Retains all counts and the mountains’ extraordinary material.
6:2|The first chariot had red horses, and the second had black horses.|Keeps the exact order and colors.
6:3|The third had white horses, and the fourth had strong, dappled horses.|Preserves strength alongside the fourth team’s color pattern.
6:4|I asked the angel speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”|Retains the recurring request for interpretation.

6:5|The angel answered, “These are the four winds of heaven, going out after standing before the Lord of all the earth.|Chooses winds with spirits as an alternative in the note, and retains their prior attendance.

6:6|The black horses are going to the northern land; the white horses follow them. The dappled horses are going to the southern land.”|Follows behind-them rather than a conjectured western destination.

6:7|The strong horses came out, eager to patrol the earth. He said, “Go, patrol the earth.” So they patrolled the earth.|Retains the threefold patrol language and leaves the unnamed commander unnamed.

6:8|Then he called out to me, “Look, those going to the northern land have brought my spirit to rest in the northern land.”|Preserves spirit/rest and the repeated destination without collapsing the image to anger alone.
6:9|The word of the LORD came to me:|Keeps the new oracle introduction.

6:10|“Take gifts from the exiles—from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon. Go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.|Clarifies the donors and destination while retaining all four names and Babylon.
6:11|Take silver and gold, make crowns, and place them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.|Retains the plural crowns and the named priest rather than substituting Zerubbabel.
6:12|Tell him: The LORD of Armies says, ‘Here is a man whose name is Branch. He will branch out from his place and build the LORD’s temple.|Keeps the Branch/branch wordplay and building task.

6:13|He will build the LORD’s temple. He will bear majesty and sit and rule on his throne. A priest will be at his throne, and peaceful counsel will be between the two of them.’|Preserves the two figures permitted by the final clause and notes the priest-on-throne alternative.

6:14|The crowns will remain in the LORD’s temple as a memorial for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.|Retains the names as written here instead of harmonizing Helem/Hen with verse ten.

6:15|Those far away will come and build in the LORD’s temple. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me to you. This will happen if you faithfully listen to the voice of the LORD your God.”|Preserves the distant builders and the explicit closing condition.
7:1|In King Darius’s fourth year, on the fourth day of the ninth month, Kislev, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah.|Retains full dating without an inferred modern date.
7:2|Bethel had sent Sharezer, Regem-melech, and his men to seek the LORD’s favor|Reads Bethel as sending community while flagging the alternate proper-name grouping.

7:3|and to ask the priests of the house of the LORD of Armies and the prophets, “Should I mourn and abstain in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?”|Keeps the singular representative question and abstinence without narrowing it beyond the context.
7:4|The word of the LORD of Armies came to me:|Preserves the shift to the prophet’s first person.

7:5|“Tell all the people of the land and the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months for these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?|Retains both fast months, seventy years, and emphatic for-me question.
7:6|And when you eat and drink, are you not eating and drinking for yourselves?|Keeps the parallel question rather than converting it to a general rule about fasting.

7:7|Are these not the words the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were inhabited and at ease, and the Negev and the lowlands were inhabited?”|Retains earlier prophetic continuity and all inhabited regions.
7:8|The word of the LORD came to Zechariah:|Keeps the renewed third-person messenger formula.
7:9|“The LORD of Armies says: Judge with true justice. Show faithful kindness and compassion to one another.|Preserves justice, hesed, and compassion as distinct obligations.

7:10|Do not oppress the widow, the fatherless, the resident foreigner, or the poor. Do not plan harm against one another in your hearts.”|Retains every vulnerable group and the interior planning prohibition.
7:11|But they refused to pay attention. They turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears from hearing.|Keeps the bodily refusal images in readable language.

7:12|They made their hearts hard as flint, refusing to hear the instruction and words the LORD of Armies had sent by his spirit through the earlier prophets. So great anger came from the LORD of Armies.|Preserves flint, spirit-mediated words, and the repeated divine title.
7:13|“Just as he called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen,” says the LORD of Armies.|Retains the he/I shift and the reciprocal refusal.

7:14|“I scattered them like a storm among nations they had not known. The land was left desolate behind them, with no one going out or returning. They made a desirable land into a wasteland.”|Keeps storm scattering, emptied movement, and their responsibility for devastation.
8:1|The word of the LORD of Armies came:|Preserves the source’s absent personal recipient.
8:2|The LORD of Armies says, “I am deeply jealous for Zion; with great fury I am jealous for her.”|Retains repeated jealousy and fury without softening the emotion.

8:3|The LORD says, “I have returned to Zion and will dwell within Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Faithfulness, and the mountain of the LORD of Armies, the Holy Mountain.”|Keeps both promised names and return/dwelling language.

8:4|The LORD of Armies says, “Old men and old women will again sit in Jerusalem’s squares, each with a staff in hand because of their great age.|Preserves both genders, staffs, and longevity as concrete signs of restored life.
8:5|The city’s squares will be full of boys and girls playing there.”|Keeps boys and girls distinct and the shared public space.

8:6|The LORD of Armies says, “If this seems impossible to the remnant of these people in those days, must it seem impossible to me?” declares the LORD of Armies.|Preserves the question and both divine-title occurrences.
8:7|The LORD of Armies says, “I will save my people from the eastern land and from the land of the setting sun.|Retains the east/west imagery rather than replacing it with all lands.

8:8|I will bring them back, and they will live within Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God in faithfulness and righteousness.”|Preserves the covenant relationship and both qualifying terms.

8:9|The LORD of Armies says, “Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words from the prophets who spoke when the foundation of the house of the LORD of Armies was laid, for the temple to be built.|Keeps hands imagery and links encouragement to the foundational prophetic words.

8:10|Before those days there were no wages for people or payment for animals. No one could come or go safely because of the enemy, and I set everyone against their neighbor.|Retains unpaid human/animal labor, unsafe travel, and divine agency in conflict.
8:11|But now I will not deal with the remnant of these people as in the former days,” declares the LORD of Armies.|Preserves the temporal reversal rather than omitting the comparison.

8:12|“For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will yield its fruit, the earth its produce, and the heavens their dew. I will give the remnant of these people all these things as an inheritance.|Keeps the seed/peace phrase and three sources of fertility.

8:13|Just as you became a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will become a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.”|Retains both houses, curse/blessing reversal, and repeated strong-hands command.

8:14|For the LORD of Armies says, “Just as I planned to bring harm on you when your ancestors provoked me to anger,” says the LORD of Armies, “and did not relent,|Retains divine intention and non-relenting as the first half of the comparison.
8:15|so in these days I have again planned to do good to Jerusalem and the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.|Completes the harm/good comparison and repeats the reassurance.
8:16|These are the things you must do: speak truth to one another; in your gates, judge with truth and judgments that bring peace.|Preserves gates as the place of judgment and both truth occurrences.
8:17|Do not plan harm against your neighbor in your hearts, and do not love false oaths. I hate all these things,” declares the LORD.|Keeps interior harm, false oaths, and divine hatred explicit.
8:18|The word of the LORD of Armies came to me:|Retains the new first-person message introduction.

8:19|The LORD of Armies says, “The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become joy, gladness, and good festivals for the house of Judah. So love truth and peace.”|Preserves all four numbered fasts and their transformation into celebration.
8:20|The LORD of Armies says, “Peoples and residents of many cities will yet come.|Keeps both peoples and cities in the gathering promise.

8:21|Residents of one city will go to another and say, ‘Let us go at once to seek the LORD’s favor and to seek the LORD of Armies. I too will go!’|Retains repeated seeking and the individual joining response.
8:22|Many peoples and powerful nations will come to seek the LORD of Armies in Jerusalem and to seek the LORD’s favor.”|Keeps both titles, Jerusalem destination, and repeated seek pattern.

8:23|The LORD of Armies says, “In those days ten men from every language of the nations will grasp the edge of a Jewish man’s garment and say, ‘Let us go with you, because we have heard that God is with you.’”|Preserves ten, male referents, garment edge, and the plural you in its communal context.

9:1|An oracle: the word of the LORD against the land of Hadrach,
with Damascus its resting place.
For the eye of humanity and of all Israel’s tribes
is toward the LORD,|Follows the human-eye direction in the difficult clause and notes the alternative divine-eye construction.
9:2|and against Hamath on its border,\nTyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.|Continues the oracle’s geography without inventing a fresh subject.
9:3|Tyre built herself a fortress\nand piled up silver like dust,\ngold like mud in the streets.|Retains the fortress and two wealth comparisons.
9:4|Look, the Lord will dispossess her\nand strike her strength into the sea;\nshe will be consumed by fire.|Keeps dispossession, sea, and fire as successive images.

9:5|Ashkelon will see and be afraid;
Gaza will writhe in anguish,
and Ekron too, because her hope has failed.
Gaza will lose her king,
and Ashkelon will no longer be inhabited.|Preserves each city and its particular consequence.
9:6|A mixed people will settle in Ashdod.\n“I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.|Renders the difficult social designation provisionally, noting its birth-status connotation.

9:7|I will remove the blood from his mouth
and the abominations from between his teeth.
He too will remain for our God
and become like a clan leader in Judah,
and Ekron like the Jebusite.|Preserves the singular personified Philistine and the incorporation language without harmonizing our God.

9:8|I will camp by my house as a guard
against those passing back and forth.
No oppressor will pass over them again,
for now I have seen with my own eyes.”|Keeps divine encampment, recurring passage, and eyes rather than abstract protection alone.

9:9|Celebrate greatly, daughter Zion!
Shout, daughter Jerusalem!
Your king is coming to you,
righteous and saved,
humble and riding on a donkey,
on a colt, the foal of a donkey.|Preserves the passive saved reading and the humble rider; notes victorious alternative without importing Matthew’s wording.

9:10|“I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim
and the warhorse from Jerusalem;
the battle bow will be cut off.
He will speak peace to the nations.
His rule will reach from sea to sea,
from the River to the ends of the earth.|Retains divine I versus king he, disarmament, and the full geographical formula.
9:11|As for you, because of the blood of your covenant\nI have released your prisoners\nfrom the waterless pit.|Keeps covenant blood and concrete pit imagery.
9:12|Return to the stronghold, prisoners of hope!\nEven today I declare:\nI will restore double to you.|Preserves the striking prisoners-of-hope phrase and double restoration.

9:13|For I have bent Judah as my bow
and fitted Ephraim to it.
I will rouse your sons, Zion,
against your sons, Greece,
and make you like a warrior’s sword.”|Retains both named combatants, sons, and the bow/sword transformation.

9:14|The LORD will appear over them;
his arrow will flash like lightning.
The Lord GOD will sound the horn
and advance in the storms of the south.|Preserves distinct divine designations and storm-warrior images.

9:15|The LORD of Armies will shield them.
They will devour and trample slingstones;
they will drink and roar as with wine.
They will be full like a sacrificial bowl,
like the corners of an altar.|Retains the difficult devouring/trampling objects and sacrificial imagery without supplying unstated blood.

9:16|The LORD their God will save them on that day,
the flock of his people.
They will be jewels in a crown,
gleaming over his land.|Keeps both flock and crown metaphors rather than choosing one.

9:17|How great its goodness! How great its beauty!\nGrain will make the young men flourish,\nand new wine the young women.|Keeps gendered parallel flourishing and notes the uncertain singular referent.

10:1|Ask the LORD for rain in the season of spring rain.
The LORD makes storm clouds;
he gives them showers of rain,
plants in the field for everyone.|Retains both divine names and seasonal agricultural context.

10:2|For the household gods speak nonsense,
the diviners see lies;
they tell empty dreams and offer empty comfort.
So the people wander like sheep,
afflicted because there is no shepherd.|Keeps all false-guidance forms and the resulting shepherdless flock.

10:3|“My anger burns against the shepherds;
I will punish the leading goats.”
For the LORD of Armies attends to his flock, the house of Judah,
and makes them like his majestic warhorse.|Preserves goats as leaders and the surprising shift from flock to warhorse.

10:5|They will be like warriors
trampling the mud of the streets in battle.
They will fight because the LORD is with them,
and horsemen will be put to shame.|Keeps the street-mud action without supplying an absent object and preserves the cause of victory.

10:6|“I will strengthen the house of Judah
and save the house of Joseph.
I will bring them back because I have compassion on them;
they will be as though I had not rejected them.
For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.|Retains both houses, compassion, reversal of rejection, and divine answer.
10:8|I will whistle for them and gather them,\nfor I have redeemed them.\nThey will be as numerous as before.|Keeps the whistle and redemption rather than reducing them to a generic summons.
10:9|I will sow them among the peoples,\nand in distant lands they will remember me.\nThey will live with their children and return.|Preserves the sowing metaphor, future sequence, and children.

10:10|I will bring them back from Egypt
and gather them from Assyria.
I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon,
until there is no room for them.|Retains all four geographical names and the implied room in the final clause.

10:11|He will pass through the sea of distress
and strike the waves of the sea;
all the depths of the Nile will dry up.
Assyria’s pride will be brought down,
and Egypt’s scepter will depart.|Preserves the third-person agent and sea-of-distress reading with ambiguity noted.
10:12|I will strengthen them in the LORD,\nand they will walk in his name,”\ndeclares the LORD.|Keeps I/LORD/his shifts and the walk-in-name idiom.
11:1|Open your doors, Lebanon,\nso fire may consume your cedars!|Keeps the command to the land and its iconic trees.

11:2|Wail, cypress, for the cedar has fallen;
the majestic trees are ruined.
Wail, oaks of Bashan,
for the dense forest has been brought down!|Retains the two laments, named region, and read dense-forest form.

11:3|Listen—the shepherds wail,
for their splendor is ruined.
Listen—the young lions roar,
for the pride of the Jordan is ruined.|Keeps repeated listen and ruined, linking shepherds and lions without explaining all referents.
11:4|The LORD my God says, “Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.|Preserves the command’s disturbing object and divine source.

11:5|Their buyers kill them and go unpunished. Their sellers say, ‘Blessed be the LORD! I am rich!’ Their own shepherds have no pity on them.|Retains buyers, sellers, and shepherds as distinct perpetrators and the profiteer’s religious speech.

11:6|For I will no longer pity the people of the land,” declares the LORD. “I will hand each person over to his neighbor and his king. They will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their hands.”|Preserves relinquished protection and the two human agents of oppression.

11:7|So I shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs, naming one Favor and the other Bonds, and shepherded the flock.|Follows the afflicted-flock wording rather than an emended merchant reading; keeps both staff names.
11:8|I removed the three shepherds in one month. I lost patience with them, and they too loathed me.|Retains the unexplained three shepherds, exact duration, and mutual alienation.
11:9|I said, “I will no longer shepherd you. Let the dying die and the perishing perish. Let those left eat one another’s flesh.”|Keeps the harsh abandonment and cannibalistic image explicit.

12:12|The land will mourn, clan by clan, each apart: David’s clan apart and their wives apart; Nathan’s clan apart and their wives apart;|Keeps named families and repeated separation of wives.

13:1|On that day a fountain will be opened for David’s house and Jerusalem’s people, for sin and impurity.|Keeps fountain and both cleansing concerns without changing the physical image to an explanation.

14:1|Look, a day belonging to the LORD is coming, when your plunder will be divided within you.|Keeps the unusual belonging-to-LORD expression and direct address to the city.
